texts.label: A
texts.title: Kingsford District Council — waste and recycling

paragraphs.text: Kingsford District Council — household waste and recycling. Bins are emptied every two weeks on the day printed on your calendar, and the two colours alternate: green for garden and food waste one week, blue for paper, glass, tins and clean plastic the next. Grey bins for everything else are emptied weekly. Please put bins out by 6.30 am on collection day and bring them back in by the end of the day; bins left on the pavement overnight may be tagged by wardens.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Crews will not empty a bin whose lid does not close, and they will not take bags left beside it. If your collection is missed through our fault, report it within two working days and we will return; if the bin was put out late, the next collection is the ordinary one. Broken bins are replaced free of charge once every five years, and an extra bin for households of six or more can be requested online at no cost.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Larger items are not taken from the kerbside. Furniture, mattresses and electrical goods must be booked for a special collection, which costs £18 for up to three items and is usually made within ten days. Garden waste in bags is accepted at the Hill Road depot, open Thursday to Sunday, 9 am to 4 pm. Paint, batteries and engine oil cannot go in any bin and are taken only at the depot, where staff will show you where to put them.
paragraphs.label: C

texts.label: B
texts.title: Brook Hall Community Centre — evening classes

paragraphs.text: Brook Hall Community Centre — autumn evening classes. Courses run for ten weeks from 15 September, on weekday evenings between 6.30 pm and 9 pm. This term we offer conversational Spanish, upholstery, sourdough baking, chair yoga, beginners’ guitar and an introduction to local history. Most classes are held in the main hall or the annexe; the baking course uses the kitchen and is limited to eight places because of the number of ovens.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Fees are £90 for the term, or £60 for people aged over 65 and for anyone receiving benefits, and they include materials except for the upholstery course, where students buy their own fabric. Payment is made in full at enrolment or in two instalments, the second due before week five. A place is not held until the first payment is received. If a course is cancelled by us because too few people enrol, fees are refunded in full within fourteen days.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Enrolment opens on 1 September in person at the reception desk and by telephone; online enrolment is not available this term. Trial classes are not offered, but you may transfer to another course of the same price during the first two weeks if a place is free. Tea and coffee are available in the foyer from 6 pm. The centre has a small car park, which fills quickly on Tuesdays when the hall is also used by the choir.
paragraphs.label: C
